questions.q: A truck uses 54 litres of diesel to travel 297 km. Assuming direct proportion, how much diesel is required for 550 km?
questions.explanation: Diesel used and distance travelled vary directly when mileage is fixed. Set 54/297 = x/550, so x = 54 x 550 / 297. Since 297 = 54 x 5.5, the result is x = 100 litres.

questions.q: A car travels a fixed journey in 10 hours at 48 km/h. What speed is needed to cover the same journey in 8 hours?
questions.explanation: For a fixed distance, speed and time vary inversely. The distance is 48 x 10 = 480 km. To cover 480 km in 8 hours, the speed must be 480/8 = 60 km/h.

questions.q: A camp has food for 300 cadets for 42 days. If 50 more cadets join, for how many days will the food last?
questions.explanation: The number of cadets and the number of days are inversely proportional for a fixed food supply. Thus 300 x 42 = 350 x d. Solving gives d = 300 x 42 / 350 = 36 days.

questions.q: At constant temperature, a gas has volume 630 cm3 at pressure 360 mm of mercury. If its volume becomes 720 cm3, what is the new pressure?
questions.explanation: At constant temperature, gas volume and pressure vary inversely, so their product remains constant. Hence 630 x 360 = 720 x p. Dividing by 720 gives p = 315 mm of mercury.
